Docs mode A = end user's own résumé/letter PDFs; B = cover-letter-framework only at `/workspace/cover-letter-framework` or `$CLC_REPO` after THAT end user installs it. DATA ISOLATION (hard rule): Never read, copy, cite, or reuse another operator's personal apply data on this shared computer. Forbidden paths include `/workspace/handshake-docs/`, `/workspace/Cover-Letter-Creator/` (and any `applications/` folders, résumés, transcripts, submit logs, hunt lists under those trees), and any file whose name or contents are clearly another person's (e.g. personal cover letters/résumés). Use only the current end user's uploads plus their own `cover-letter-framework` pr

skills.name: Handshake Application Tracker
skills.description: Use when logging Handshake applications to a spreadsheet or syncing apply status changes.
skills.content:
---
name: Handshake Application Tracker
description: >-
  Use when logging Handshake applications to a spreadsheet or syncing apply
  status changes.
---
# Handshake Application Tracker

Keep a running log of Handshake applications and surface status changes.

## Inputs
- The user's applications spreadsheet, if they already have one. If they do not, create a Google Sheet titled "Handshake Applications" (or the name they give) with columns: Date applied, Company, Title, Source, Status, Notes.
- New applies from a live run, a routine, or Handshake's applications list.

## Access
Prefer Google Sheets (and Drive to create the file) when those connectors are connected. Prefer a Handshake connector for application status if one is usable; otherwise read Handshake Applications in the signed-in browser.

## Steps
1. Resolve the tracker spreadsheet. Reuse the existing one; do not create a duplicate.
2. After each successful Handshake apply, append a row: date in the user's timezone (YYYY-MM-DD), company, title, source `Handshake`, status `Applied`, short notes (Easy Apply, Quick apply, skipped questions, and so on).
3. Skip the row if that company + title is already listed.
4. When asked to sync, open Handshake's applications / history view and update Status for rows that changed (viewed, interview, rejected, offer). Do not invent statuses you did not see.
5. Report new rows and any status changes, and link the sheet.

## Hard rules
- Never fabricate applications or status changes.
- Do not log skipped or external-ATS jobs as applied.
- Do not overwrite existing notes unless you are clearly correcting a status.

  attending, who matches the search, talking points, RSVP.
---
# Handshake Career Fair Brief

Prepare the user for a Handshake career fair or campus recruiting event.

## Inputs
- Which event, school, or date if they named one. Otherwise use the next Handshake event they are eligible for.
- Their job-search intent and resume highlights (from profile or resume file).

## Access
Prefer a Handshake connector for events if usable. Otherwise use the signed-in Handshake Events page in the browser. If logged out, hand them the computer to sign in.

## Steps
1. Find the event on Handshake (name, date, location, RSVP state).
2. List attending employers that match their search. Cap at a short target list (about 8–12), each with one line on why they fit.
3. For the top 3, write 3 talking points grounded only in their real resume and the employer's Handshake page. No invented projects or metrics.
4. RSVP only if they asked to RSVP. Otherwise say whether they are already registered and offer to RSVP.
5. Deliver a night-before brief: event logistics, target list, talking points, and any open Handshake messages from those employers.

## Hard rules
- Do not RSVP or message employers unless they asked.
- Do not invent employer facts you did not see on Handshake.
- If no matching event exists, say so in one line.

  Easy Apply / in-Handshake apply only.
---
# Handshake Match and Easy Apply

Find Handshake jobs that match the user's search, then apply only when the application stays on Handshake.

## Inputs
- Search intent (role, location, job type, keywords). If missing, use their current Handshake job search.
- Resume already on their Handshake profile, or a resume file they have named.
- Standing answers they have confirmed (for example work authorization or visa sponsorship). Never invent answers they have not confirmed.

## Access
Prefer a Handshake connector if one is connected and usable. If not, use the signed-in Handshake session in the browser. If the session is logged out, 2FA, or captcha, hand them the computer to sign in and stop.

## Steps
1. Open Handshake student Jobs. Reuse their existing search when they have one.
2. Collect a short ranked list of matches (title, company, location, why it fits). Prefer internships or roles that match the stated intent.
3. For each candidate, open Apply. Continue only if the flow stays on Handshake (Easy Apply / in-app). Skip already-applied jobs and any apply that redirects to an external ATS or company site.
4. Submit with the resume on their profile. Answer only questions they have already confirmed. Skip a job if it needs a cover letter, essay, or screening answers you cannot take from the profile or resume.
5. Cap applies unless they named a different number (default 10 for a scheduled sweep, 3 for an ad-hoc "apply to a few").
6. Report what was applied and what was skipped (and why). If an application tracker skill or spreadsheet exists, log successful applies there.

## Hard rules
- In-Handshake apply only. No Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, or company-site forms.
- Do not invent employment history, GPA, essays, or work-auth / sponsorship answers.
- Do not apply outside this skill unless they explicitly asked for a live run.

skills.description: Use when new Handshake recruiter messages need a draft reply in the user's voice. Never send without confirmation.

  Use when new Handshake recruiter messages need a draft reply in the user's
  voice. Never send without confirmation.
---
# Handshake Recruiter Reply Drafts

Draft replies to Handshake recruiter messages in the user's voice. Do not send until they confirm.

## Inputs
- New threads in Handshake Inbox, or a specific message they pointed at.
- A sample of their recent sent messages in that same inbox (or the channel they asked you to match) so the draft sounds like them.

## Access
Prefer a Handshake connector for inbox read/draft if usable. Otherwise use the signed-in Handshake Inbox in the browser. If a connector would send as an app instead of as the user, draft in chat and send only through the signed-in browser after they confirm.

## Steps
1. List new recruiter threads: who, company, one-line ask, waiting on them or not.
2. For each thread that needs a reply, read the full thread and draft one short reply.
3. Match their register (offer to sample recent sent mail in that inbox first).
4. Show drafts in chat. Wait for an explicit send/edit/skip on each one.
5. After they confirm, send only those they approved. Log anything that should hit the application tracker (interview scheduled, withdrew, and so on).

## Hard rules
- Never send or reply without explicit confirmation.
- Never invent availability, compensation, work authorization, or experience.
- If the thread needs a fact you do not have, ask them instead of guessing.

skills.name: Handshake Resume Gap Check
skills.description: Use when comparing the user's resume to a Handshake posting to flag real gaps. Never invent experience.
skills.content:
---
name: Handshake Resume Gap Check
description: >-
  Use when comparing the user's resume to a Handshake posting to flag real gaps.
  Never invent experience.
---
# Handshake Resume Gap Check

Compare the user's resume to a Handshake job posting and flag real gaps.

## Inputs
- The job (URL, Handshake search result, or pasted description).
- Their current resume (Handshake profile resume or the file they named).

## Access
Read the posting from Handshake (connector or signed-in browser). Read the resume from the file or Handshake profile. Do not edit the resume unless they asked for a revision.

## Steps
1. Pull required and preferred qualifications from the posting only.
2. Map each qualification to evidence on the resume (role, project, tool, or date). Mark as met, partial, or missing.
3. Call out the biggest 3–5 gaps and what honest edit could close them (reorder, clarify an existing role, add a real project they already have).
4. If they want a revised resume, edit only from facts they already have. Show the diff in words before saving a new file.
5. Do not apply to the job unless they also asked to apply.

## Hard rules
- Never invent employers, titles, metrics, skills, GPA, or coursework.
- If they asked to skip GPA or other fields, leave those out of the resume and the gap list unless the posting makes them required — then flag the conflict instead of filling it in.
- Partial matches stay partial. Do not stretch.
